issue.description:
ADR-004's decision commits to a `cargo +1.85 check --all-targets` lane in `bead-rs-ci` so the declared Rust 1.85 floor is tested on every run 'instead of asserted', and requires that drift between the lane's pinned toolchain and the manifest's `rust-version` be a CI failure. No open bead covers this lane (the only visible CI bead is arch-suffixed release publishing). Work: verify whether the lane already exists in the applied workflow template; if absent or unpinned, add it pinned to exactly the manifest's `rust-version`, plus a check that fails when the two diverge. Without it the MSRV claim is true only by luck and any dependency refresh can silently break the floor.

---
Priority: P3
Created by: weave strand
issue.title: Add the pinned MSRV verification lane to bead-rs-ci with manifest drift as a failure (ADR-004)

issue.description:
Add bead sync fork: an explicit operator command that re-origins a cloned workspace under a new store UUID recorded in a provenance-chained receipt, so clones of one repository become distinct origins whose event streams merge composably under existing different-UUID rules instead of being rejected as same-UUID divergence.

Acceptance:
- fork receipt fields and UUID derivation provenance specified
- forked clone merges into the origin workspace cleanly via existing merge rules
- doctor detects same-UUID divergence and names the fork/reconcile remedy
- forking is never implicit or inferred

Refs: plan section 12 R028; ideas-ledger 2026-08-15 finalist 2.

issue.description:
Parent: beadrs-8c343a7c (claim-epoch fencing umbrella). Child 4 of 5 - lock the whole contract in with deterministic tests, including the original incident sequence.

Scope:
- Write the deterministic two-connection test: A claims epoch 1; an explicit reason-bearing recovery releases epoch 1; B claims epoch 2. Every A attempt (update, release, close, reopen, resource-lock change, atomic attempt resolve) with epoch 1 conflicts with exit code 4 and B remains assigned and in_progress.
- Write the companion positive test: the same operations from B with epoch 2 succeed.
- Test that omitting the credential on a claimed issue conflicts unless the explicit audited operator override with a reason is used.
- Cover both leased and non-leased claim paths, and prove historical lease rows never brick a later valid epoch.
- Keep the twenty-way simultaneous claim coverage proving exactly one successful claimant per issue.
- Cover the conflict boundary: a conflicting mutation leaves revision, audit events, resource locks, attempt receipts, and checkpoint state exactly as they were.
- Add an installed-CLI integration fixture reproducing the spaxel incident sequence: live claimant, external release, new claimant, then stale claimant mutation.

Acceptance:
- New tests are deterministic (no sleep-dependent timing) and pass on repeated runs of the concurrency and stress suites.
- cargo fmt --check, cargo clippy --all-targets -- -D warnings, and cargo test pass.
issue.title: Add deterministic claim-epoch fencing concurrency regression tests

issue.close_reason:
Verified the superseded-credential rejection on the update path against the landed code. No gap found, no source change needed, so no fmt/clippy run was required.

Commit verified against: 89c72165f391a395e0b4d1b911a0a86a96254a37 (origin/main tip; the fence itself landed in 7addba812f18b24f0a409cd8b188fd8031ba5f84).

Test summary: cargo test --test claim_epoch -> test result: ok. 9 passed; 0 failed; 0 ignored; finished in 5.05s. Includes a_superseded_credential_cannot_mutate_the_claim_that_replaced_it ... ok, which sweeps update/release/close/reopen/resource add/resource remove/resolve with a superseded epoch, asserting exit 4 plus the Claim-epoch credential message (not just any non-zero exit), held_state unchanged, and no published event -- then the current holder's update with the current epoch.

Mutation control (proves the test is wired to the guard rather than passing vacuously): with validate_claim_epoch_for_mutation short-circuited to Ok(()), the named test FAILED at tests/claim_epoch.rs:128 -- "update with the superseded credential must conflict with exit 4, got Some(0)" -- the stale update succeeded once the guard was gone. Restored byte-for-byte (src/service/leases.rs sha256 1591581bf2e305f0918699695c02228ee5e9b7a51c3ef045dde29e7b451fae40), worktree clean for that path.

Independent manual probe on the freshly built binary (bead 0.2.6 built from this checkout): a superseded credential (epoch 1) on update -> exit 4, "Lease conflict: Claim-epoch credential mismatch: issue ... is claimed at claim epoch 2, not 1"; status/assignee/revision unchanged (in_progress/worker-two/4) and checkpoint event count unchanged (4 -> 4), i.e. no write, no revision bump, no published event, and the claim still belongs to the current holder. The current holder with epoch 2 -> exit 0, notes actually landed, revision 4 -> 5, assignee still worker-two.

Implementation: src/service/lifecycle.rs:239 gates update_issue_in_tx inside the caller's transaction and before the only write at line 255; src/service/leases.rs:420 returns Error::LeaseConflict, mapped to exit 4 at src/error.rs:135.
issue.description:
Child in the replacement auto-split of beadrs-9cdb17cf (itself child 1 of 5 under beadrs-a6554831). An earlier 4-child chain for this same parent (beadrs-46ced453, beadrs-da4fae12, beadrs-57a448b2, beadrs-9ddc6f45) was closed evidence-free by the Phase 19.4 sweeper at 17:09:16Z and again at 17:16:41Z on 2026-09-05; those titles are immutable and start with the sweeper's attractor word, so these replacements carry resistant titles and put the commands in the body.

Context: the update-path credential fence is believed already landed in commit 7addba8 on origin/main. The deliverable is independent verification of this one slice against the landed code, or the smallest possible fix if a gap is found. Re-implementing from scratch is not wanted.

Scope: a credential minted by a superseded claim epoch is refused on the update path with exit code 4 and leaves the CURRENT claim fully intact: no write, no revision bump, no published event, and the claim still belongs to the current holder. The current holder presenting the exact current epoch still lands its update.

Acceptance:
- cargo test --test claim_epoch passes, with a_superseded_credential_cannot_mutate_the_claim_that_replaced_it demonstrating the stale-credential refusal on update and then the current holder's successful update.
- Close reason carries the evidence: test summary line (N passed / 0 failed), the commit SHA verified against, and fmt/clippy results if any source change was needed.
issue.notes: Verified the superseded-credential rejection on the update path at 89c7216: no gap found, no source change needed. cargo test --test claim_epoch: 9 passed / 0 failed, including a_superseded_credential_cannot_mutate_the_claim_that_replaced_it. Mutation control confirms the test genuinely detects an update-path hole (guard disabled -> stale update exits 0 instead of 4). Full evidence in the close reason.
issue.title: Audit the superseded-credential rejection on the update path
